markdown_report:
The recommended first experiment is **position-dependent gating over NextItNet dilation depths**, trained jointly within one model per category. This is a hypothesis; no validation improvement has been measured.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Users report that older, isolated purchases overshadow coherent recent behavior. Adaptive context length could reduce this mismatch. (2) Broadly related recommendations displace specific purpose or mood matches. Selecting contextual scale may sharpen immediate intent, but cannot establish product compatibility. (3) Electronics has 12.27% sampled ranking errors and a −0.2595 lower-tail margin. Embedding similarity near 0.5 does not indicate strong directional collapse, making contextual discrimination a more defensible target than embedding dispersion.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [NextItNet](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf) expands context through causal dilations. [TV-Rec](https://openreview.net/pdf/e9c3bd1680a3ab54ffe119fc526e57d9835d7b8d.pdf) motivates adaptive convolutional processing, without proving gains here. (2) [Sampled-softmax research](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) connects temperature with negative-example emphasis. This motivates moderate multi-negative objectives as a separate experiment. (3) [Semantic fusion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18166) motivates distinguishing text and ID representations. Its findings do not establish that scratch-trained text will resolve practical fit.

**Framework and candidate directions.** Context selection addresses stale intent; objective design addresses confusing candidates; content integration addresses item identity. These mechanisms target different information gaps.

Scores are 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each cell gives a score and one positive/negative consideration. Alignment scores describe hypotheses, not observed gains.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Learned dilation-depth gates | 5: conditional scale selection / familiar mechanism | 7: adaptable context / may retain stale cues | 8: recent purpose and stale interests / cannot verify fit | 7: contextual discrimination / margins may remain weak | 3: small module / predictor changes |
| Moderate-temperature multi-negative loss | 3: established objective / little novelty | 7: better candidate competition / false negatives remain | 5: finer ranking / no explicit intent control | 9: targets weak separation / sampled gains may not generalize | 4: reusable scoring / exclusion bookkeeping |
| Joint scratch-trained title/ID gate | 5: constrained fusion / established ingredients | 6: identifiable item cues / sparse text supervision | 7: specificity / similarity is not compatibility | 6: extra discrimination / noisy features | 6: no external weights / tokenization overhead |

**Selected algorithm.** At 0% progress, dilation gates offer a small, testable change. They explicitly address two reported failures: persistent influence from isolated older interactions and broad matches displacing recent purpose-specific matches. They also target Electronics’ weak contextual separation, without promising improvements.

Retain causal residual blocks and expose their intermediate features. At each position, learn softmax weights over projected block outputs and use their weighted feature in the existing next-item objective. Keep the objective and other hyperparameters fixed initially to isolate the mechanism.

Compare with the corrected baseline using fixed four-category macro validation HR@10. Preserve seeds, 200 epochs maximum, 200 batches/epoch, routing, diagnostic interfaces, and one checkpoint/category. Read the final nonpadding position; serialize the identical architecture in the predictor writer.

idea.description: Add jointly learned, position-dependent gates over intermediate dilation-depth features within the supplied NextItNet backbone.
idea.motivation: Test whether adaptive contextual scale reduces stale-interest persistence and broad-purpose mismatches while improving the weak positive-negative separation measured in Electronics. Compatibility, duplication avoidance, and HR@10 improvements remain unproven.
idea.implementation_notes: Keep the corrected baseline objective, sampler, optimizer, and other hyperparameters unchanged for the initial comparison. Project intermediate causal block outputs into a common feature space, compute position-wise softmax gates, and form one weighted feature representation. All components belong to one jointly trained network; use one selected checkpoint per category. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and write artifacts beneath the trial directory. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four datasets, supplied splits, maximum 200 epochs, and 200 batches per epoch. Preserve ModelView.item_emb, log2feats(sequence), and predict_score(features, items). Keep DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis); report measured margins with their definitions and mark unavailable metadata breakdowns unavailable. Update the embedded predictor writer with the exact model definition and checkpoint configuration. No timestamp or unavailable metadata input is required. No executable patch is supplied because the corrected baseline source is absent from the prompt.
idea.pseudocode:
x = item_emb(sequence)
valid = sequence != 0
states = []
for block, projection in zip(causal_residual_blocks, projections):
    x = block(x) * valid[..., None]
    states.append(projection(x) * valid[..., None])
H = stack(states, dim=2)                  # B,L,K,D
gate_logits = gate(concat(states, dim=-1)) # B,L,K
weights = softmax(gate_logits, dim=-1)
features = layer_norm(sum(weights[..., None] * H, dim=2))
features = features * valid[..., None]
loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(features, positive, negative)
# Inference:
last = maximum_position_where(sequence != 0)  # never count-1
scores = predict_score(features[batch_index, last], candidates)
# Handle empty histories using the corrected baseline's existing policy.

originality.positive: Applies conditional selection of contextual scale to the observed NextItNet failure patterns.
originality.negative: Feature gating and multiscale aggregation are established techniques.

future_potential.positive: Provides a compact basis for studying when short or extended interaction context helps recommendation.
future_potential.negative: Gate weights alone cannot establish current intent or causal explanations for recommendations.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires a small jointly trained module over existing block outputs.
code_difficulty.negative: Intermediate features, checkpoint configuration, diagnostic compatibility, and predictor generation must remain consistent.

related_work.title: NextItNet
contributions: Uses residual dilated causal convolutions for sequential recommendation.
limitations: Expanded receptive fields do not explicitly determine which historical context remains relevant to the next choice.

related_work.title: TV-Rec
limitations: Does not establish that dilation-depth gating improves the supplied RecHarness benchmark.

related_work.title: Wu et al., sampled-softmax study
contributions: Analyzes how temperature changes emphasis on difficult negative examples.
limitations: Does not establish an optimal temperature or gains for the supplied NextItNet models.

related_work.title: Sequence-level Semantic Representation Fusion
contributions: Motivates accounting for differences between semantic and interaction representations.
limitations: Does not demonstrate that scratch-trained title features establish functional compatibility or improve this benchmark.
